description: Turning an organisation's operational data into decisions: framing business questions and key performance indicators, dimensional models for reporting, extract, transform and load pipelines, dashboard design, self-service analytics, reporting for managers and the governance that keeps the numbers trusted. Students build a working star schema, ETL pipeline and dashboard on simulated company data in the browser and defend every metric to a mock management team.
modelledOn: Kimball and Ross, The Data Warehouse Toolkit: The Definitive Guide to Dimensional Modeling
Few, Information Dashboard Design: Displaying Data for At-a-Glance Monitoring
Parmenter, Key Performance Indicators: Developing, Implementing and Using Winning KPIs
DAMA International, DAMA-DMBOK: Data Management Body of Knowledge
outcomes: Translate organisational goals into precise business questions and well-defined key performance indicators.
Design dimensional models with fact tables, conformed dimensions and slowly changing dimensions for reporting.
Build and test extract, transform and load pipelines that clean, integrate and incrementally load data.
Design dashboards that follow perception principles and answer the questions of a named audience.
Enable self-service analytics with a semantic layer, and write reports that lead decision makers to action.
Apply data governance, quality and privacy controls so that reported figures are trusted and lawful.

units.title: Business intelligence and decision making
topics: Operational versus analytical systems; OLTP and OLAP; the BI value chain from data to decision
Descriptive, diagnostic, predictive and prescriptive analytics
BI architectures: data warehouse, data marts, data lake and lakehouse; Inmon versus Kimball
The BI tool landscape: open-source and commercial reporting, OLAP and dashboard tools

units.title: Business questions and key performance indicators
topics: Eliciting requirements from stakeholders; turning vague goals into answerable questions
Metrics versus KPIs; leading and lagging indicators; SMART targets
Balanced scorecard and strategy maps; KPI trees linking operations to goals
Defining a KPI precisely: formula, grain, filters, owner, target, frequency and data source
Perverse incentives and Goodhart's law
KPIs for a mobile money operator: active agents, float availability, transaction value and churn

units.title: Dimensional models for reporting
topics: Kimball's four-step design: business process, grain, dimensions and facts
Star and snowflake schemas; transaction, periodic snapshot and accumulating snapshot fact tables
Additive, semi-additive and non-additive measures
Conformed dimensions and the bus matrix; the date dimension; degenerate and junk dimensions
Slowly changing dimensions types 1, 2 and 3; surrogate keys
Designing a sales star schema for a chain of pharmacies across Ghana's regions

units.title: Extract, transform and load
topics: Source systems and extraction: full, incremental and change data capture
Data profiling and cleansing: duplicates, missing values, inconsistent codes and units
Transformations: lookups, surrogate key assignment, SCD handling and aggregation
ETL versus ELT; staging areas; orchestration and scheduling of pipelines
Testing pipelines: row counts, reconciliation, data quality rules and audit columns
Handling unreliable connectivity: batching uploads from branches and idempotent loads

units.title: Querying and OLAP
topics: OLAP operations: slice, dice, drill-down, roll-up and pivot
Analytical SQL: GROUP BY with ROLLUP and CUBE, window functions, running totals and period-over-period comparisons
Cubes, aggregates and materialised views for performance
Semantic layers and calculated measures; time intelligence such as year to date

units.title: Building dashboards
topics: Strategic, operational and analytical dashboards; designing for the audience and the decision
Layout and visual hierarchy; at-a-glance monitoring; bullet graphs and sparklines
Choosing charts for KPIs; showing targets, variance and trends; avoiding gauges and clutter
Filters, drill-through and interactivity; mobile layouts and low-bandwidth delivery
Usability testing a dashboard with real users; iterating on feedback
A district health dashboard of immunisation coverage and stock-outs

units.title: Self-service analytics
topics: Self-service models: governed data sets, certified metrics and sandboxes
Designing a semantic model that business users can understand
Training and data literacy; the citizen analyst
Risks of self-service: conflicting numbers, spreadmarts and shadow IT

units.title: Reporting for decision makers
topics: Structuring a management report: the answer first, evidence, and recommended action
Variance analysis and exception reporting; commentary that explains movements
Presenting uncertainty and data limitations honestly
Scheduled reports, alerts and distribution by email, SMS and messaging apps
Presenting findings on cocoa purchasing to a licensed buying company's board

units.title: Data governance in organisations
topics: Data governance roles: owners, stewards and custodians; a data governance council
Data quality dimensions and measurement; master data and reference data management
Metadata, data catalogues, business glossaries and lineage
Security, row-level access and privacy; Ghana's Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843)
Capstone: an end-to-end BI solution with schema, pipeline, dashboard and governance plan

schedule.title: From operational data to decisions
schedule.exercise: Short written exercise: for a pharmacy chain, list five operational (OLTP) questions and five analytical (OLAP) questions, classify each as descriptive, diagnostic, predictive or prescriptive, and sketch where the data should live.

tasks.title: Run one OLTP-style lookup and one aggregate query on a sales database and explain in two sentences why the second is an analytical workload
Sort twelve manager questions into descriptive, diagnostic, predictive and prescriptive analytics and choose the evidence each would need, scored on a rubric
Draw an architecture diagram for a retail BI platform with sources, staging, warehouse, two data marts and a lake, and justify one Inmon versus Kimball choice

schedule.title: Requirements and KPI trees
schedule.exercise: Interview-style exercise: turn three vague goals from a manager into answerable questions, then build a KPI tree linking them to operations and a balanced scorecard.

tasks.title: Question a stakeholder in a branching interview to turn the vague goal 'improve service' into three measurable questions, scoring each for clarity and answerability
Classify 12 metrics for a mobile money operator as KPIs or plain metrics and as leading or lagging, and set a SMART target for four of them
Draw a KPI tree that links daily agent operations to a balanced scorecard and a strategic goal, and mark which nodes are leading indicators

schedule.title: Defining KPIs precisely
schedule.exercise: Write full KPI definition cards (formula, grain, filters, owner, target, frequency, source) for five KPIs and describe how each could be gamed.

tasks.title: Write a SQL query that implements the KPI 'active agent' with an explicit formula, grain and 30-day filter, and check the result for one region
Predict how call-centre staff will game a 'calls closed per hour' KPI, choose a better balanced set of indicators and score the redesign on a rubric
Implement active agents, float availability, transaction value and churn as queries over a mobile money table, and reconcile your totals to a supplied control figure

schedule.title: Designing a star schema
schedule.exercise: Design a star schema on paper for a hospital outpatient visit process: declare business process and grain, then list dimensions, facts and measure additivity.

tasks.title: Declare the business process, grain, dimensions and facts for a supermarket till system, then create the fact table and one dimension table in SQL
Create a star and an equivalent snowflake schema for the same sales data, load both and compare the join count and result of a monthly revenue query
Classify ten measures as additive, semi-additive or non-additive, then write queries showing that summing account balances across dates gives a wrong answer

schedule.title: Dimensions, history and the pharmacy schema
schedule.exercise: Prepare a bus matrix for a pharmacy chain and a dimension design note explaining which attributes need history and which do not.

tasks.title: Build a bus matrix of four business processes against conformed dimensions for a pharmacy chain and mark the conformed date, product and branch dimensions
Apply SCD type 1 and type 2 to a customer dimension after an address change and show with queries how each affects last year's sales by region
Design, load and query a sales star schema for pharmacies across Ghana's regions, answering five management questions and checking totals against the source system

schedule.title: Extraction and cleansing
schedule.exercise: Profile a messy export from a branch system, list its quality problems, and describe the cleaning rules and the extraction method you would use.

tasks.title: Run a full extract and an incremental extract using a last-modified timestamp from a source table and verify the incremental load picks up only changed rows
Profile a branch sales table for duplicates, missing values and inconsistent unit codes, then write cleaning queries and show before and after row counts
Transform a staged table into a dimension with lookups, surrogate keys and SCD type 2 handling, then aggregate a fact table and check reconciliation

schedule.title: Pipelines, testing and weak connectivity
schedule.exercise: Design an ELT pipeline for twenty branches uploading when the network allows, specifying schedule, tests and what happens on a failed or repeated upload.

tasks.title: Draw a pipeline diagram showing sources, staging area, load and a nightly schedule, and mark which steps follow ELT rather than ETL
Write row-count, reconciliation and data quality rule checks for a daily load and add audit columns recording load time and batch number
Make a branch upload idempotent so a batch sent three times loads once, and prove with counts after replaying a failed partial upload

schedule.title: OLAP and analytical SQL
schedule.exercise: Answer ten management questions against a sales warehouse using slice, dice, roll-up and window functions, and justify an aggregate table.

tasks.title: Perform a slice, a dice and a drill-down from year to month on a sales fact table and record the SQL for each operation
Write a query using ROLLUP for regional subtotals and window functions for running totals and month-over-month change in revenue
Create a materialised summary of monthly sales, compare query plans with and without it, and add a calculated year-to-date measure that stays correct after refresh

schedule.title: Designing dashboards
schedule.exercise: Sketch three dashboards (strategic, operational, analytical) for a mobile money operator and annotate the audience, decision and chart choices for each.

tasks.title: Match four dashboard requests to strategic, operational or analytical types and choose the right audience and refresh frequency, scored on a rubric
Lay out a one-screen operational dashboard on a wireframe with a visual hierarchy, bullet graphs and sparklines, and place the most urgent KPI top left
Critique a cluttered dashboard full of gauges, pick the chart for each KPI showing target, variance and trend, and justify every replacement

schedule.title: Interactivity and the district health dashboard
schedule.exercise: Test a dashboard prototype with two classmates, record where they struggle, and write the three changes you will make next.

tasks.title: Mock up filters, a drill-through and a low-bandwidth mobile layout for a district dashboard, listing which elements load first on a slow connection
Run a usability test scenario on a dashboard, interpret the observer notes, and choose the three most important fixes with a rubric-scored justification
Build the queries behind a district health dashboard of immunisation coverage and stock-outs and flag districts below 80 percent coverage with a stock-out

schedule.title: Self-service analytics
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page governed self-service policy: certified data sets, sandbox rules, training, and how conflicting numbers are resolved.

tasks.title: Decide which of eight data sets should be certified for self-service and which stay in a sandbox, and defend each decision on a rubric
Create views that give business users plain-named measures and dimensions for sales data, then answer three questions without writing a join
Investigate a case where two departments report different revenue totals, find the cause in the evidence provided and recommend a governance fix

schedule.title: Reporting to decision makers
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page board report in answer-first format on a purchasing variance, including commentary on the movement and a stated data limitation.

tasks.title: Reorder the parts of a management report so the answer comes first, followed by evidence and a recommended action, and score the result
Query actual against budget cocoa purchasing by month, flag exceptions beyond 10 percent and draft a one-line commentary explaining each flagged movement
Present findings on cocoa purchasing to a licensed buying company's board, choose what to show, how to state uncertainty and which action to recommend

schedule.title: Data governance and capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone deliverable: schema diagram, ETL description, dashboard sketch and a governance plan with roles, quality measures and a privacy section.

tasks.title: Assign owners, stewards and custodians to six data sets in a case file and decide the agenda for a first data governance council meeting
Measure completeness, uniqueness and validity of a customer table with SQL queries, then fix the records that fail and report the improvement
Build an end-to-end mini solution: star schema, load script with quality checks, three dashboard queries and row-level access views, then document the governance plan
